newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse trade boosted by rally after US data.
newsitem.headline: German bourse trade boosted by rally after US data.

text.p: German shares rose at the start of bourse trade on Friday to catch up with the rally that occurred post-bourse Thursday following U.S. data that calmed market fears of a U.S. interest rate increase.

The DAX-30 index of leading German shares was up 37.38 points, or 1.30 percent to 2,930.11, in mid-bourse, reflecting the surge in stocks on the Dow Jones index overnight, which closed up 1.16 percent at 6,625.67 points.
The German stock market made a strong recovery from pre-bourse electronic trade, when the IBIS DAX index fell after Japan's Nikkei-225 share index fell 4.3 percent.

The DAX index was comfortably above the psychologically-important 2,900-point level and the strong dollar at 1.5785 was seen as supporting share values. Investor focus now centred on U.S. jobs data due 1330 GMT.

The main share in the news was the carmaker Volkswagen AG, which was up 17 marks at 707.50 marks in mid-bourse trade, after it announced it had reached a settlement with General Motors in the long-running legal dispute between the two.
Another German carmaker, BMW AG, was up 23 marks at 1.076 marks on positive expectations on the group's earnings in 1996.
